clues: For centuries this coastal exposure has helped people investigate the origin of unusual rocks.
Its formations are linked to volcanic activity roughly 50 to 60 million years ago.
Tens of thousands of dark basalt columns form a pavement below coastal cliffs.
The shapes inspired stories of giants travelling across the sea towards Scotland.
On Northern Ireland’s Antrim coast, find the celebrated shore of closely packed polygonal basalt columns.
targetLabel: Giant’s Causeway and Causeway Coast — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: The columns are volcanic rock formations, while the giant stories belong to cultural interpretation. Keeping those explanations distinct makes the site useful for learning how landscapes inspire both science and folklore. The target represents the designated coastal property, not an exact stepping stone.
